title: Regional circuit breakers and backpressure protocol for quota hysteresis
creator: Anjali Mehta
description: Design and implement a regionalized circuit-breaker + backpressure protocol for quota enforcement to ensure SLO stability during limiter outages and cross-region bursts. This ticket formalizes an 'emergency local mode' that allows regions to autonomously shed load in a predictable, fair way while preserving global SLOs where possible. Focus areas: fast detection, deterministic fair-share under partial connectivity, graceful degradation to degraded quota buckets, and a clear operator runbook for recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Each region can detect limiter instability within 300ms (metric: limiter.health.failures > threshold) and transition to emergency-local-mode automatically

Emergency-local-mode enforces local quotas using deterministic fair-sharing (documentation + algorithm proof-of-concept) and reduces P99 latency impact on existing SLO tenants by >= 40% compared to uncontrolled failure

Cross-region fallback: when local mode is active, 95% of requests that previously succeeded continue to succeed with degraded token budgets (configurable), and error rate increase is limited to <= 5% for critical customers
Rollout includes automated canary (1 region, 1% traffic) and a staged global rollout with rollback automated by circuit health checks
Runbook documented with exactly three operator actions and automated escalation hooks (PagerDuty + Slack), and verified in playbook test
implementation_notes: Introduce a new limiter state machine with states: Healthy -> Degraded (soft-shed) -> EmergencyLocalMode (hard-shed) -> Recovering

Use local token buckets with lease-based borrow mechanism: regions can borrow from a small global emergency pool when connectivity is healthy; when connectivity is poor, borrow fails fast and local fallback applies
Deterministic fair-share: use per-customer weight + time-decayed deficit counter (inspired by DRF) implemented in the hot path with bounded CPU + O(1) operations
Circuit detection heuristics: combine request rejection spike, RPC latency to central quota service, and gRPC errors to avoid false positives during short spikes
Expose a 'limiter.mode' tag in all traces to make post-incident attribution straightforward
Make emergency-local-mode configurable by capacity profile and per-customer exemption lists (for high-SLA customers)
Avoid cross-region consensus for fast transitions; rely on monotonic region-local decisions with eventual reconciliation to avoid cascading failures
progress_updates: 2025-03-05: Initial design proposed; sketched state machine and emergency pool idea. Blocking: need clear SLOs from product for acceptable error uplift.
2025-03-07: SLOs aligned with PM (see PM note: limit error uplift to 5% for core customers). Started prototype of deterministic fair-share counters in Go runtime.
2025-03-09: Prototype benchmark results: additional CPU < 6% on p3.2xlarge for 1k rps; memory for counters < 20MB per-region. Integration test harness created.
2025-03-10: Engineering review scheduled; security requested review for exemption list handling (KMS requirement).
review_feedback: Security: store exemption lists encrypted at rest; require replay-protection in changesets
Observability: add a dedicated SLI for 'requests served during emergency-local-mode' and include in the console SLO dashboard
PM: make per-customer emergency quotas configurable via Console and default to conservative values for new customers
Design: clarify UX for Console toggle and show live health of regional limiters
related_dashboards: Grafana: Emergency Mode Impact - p50/p95/p99 latency during limiter events
notes_for_ops: If region enters EmergencyLocalMode, do not attempt manual global quota override unless instructed by SRE lead
To recover: ensure connectivity to central quota service, then set limiter.state to Recovering in Console to begin token reconciliation
If partial recovery: monitor 'reconcile_failures' metric and escalate if > 0.1% for 10 minutes
postmortem_learnings: From incident 2025-01-18: synchronous global locking caused cascading quota failures; new design avoids global locks in hot path
Operational complexity increased when exemption lists were not versioned; ensure change history lives in git-backed store
communication_plan: Pre-rollout: Notify customers with high SLOs via email and Console banner 72h before canary
During incident: automated Slack channel #infra-alerts and PagerDuty for engineers on-call
Post-rollout: publish summary and metrics to status.redwood.ai and update customer-facing KB
testing_plan: Unit tests for state transitions, borrow-fail-fast behavior, and fair-share invariants
Integration test: simulate regional network partition and ensure EmergencyLocalMode triggers and recovers deterministically
Canary: deploy to eu-west-1 with 1% production traffic for 48h, monitor SLI dashboards and error budget burn
Chaos test: inject gRPC error spikes and verify no single tenant experiences > 10x baseline error rate (configurable threshold)
